profile.org_note: Three homebuilding reporting segments (Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest; the 10-Q says the company is organised mainly by region) sit over roughly 27 local divisions, each led by a Division President who, per the June 2026 release, now reports up to COO Clint Szubinski; no segment-level regional president is publicly named (Liesel Cooper's 2024 regional role over Colorado and the ex-Crescent divisions is unconfirmed since), and Beazer (acquired 2026-10-20) has not yet been placed in a segment. Land deals start with divisional VPs of Land (who report to the Division President with a dotted line to a Regional VP of Land, e.g. Matt Childers for Texas/Colorado/Arizona, and to SVP of Land Batey McGraw) and are approved by the six-person Asset Management Committee (CEO Patrick Zalupski, CFO Anabel Ramsay, McGraw, National President Doug Moran, SVP Finance Michelle Murrhee, GC Robert Riva), with deals of $75M or more going to the Board and financing going to land bankers, where 49%-owned DF Capital holds a right of first offer.
profile.summary: Builder 100 #14 before the deal; after closing the ~$2.2B all-cash purchase of Beazer Homes on 2026-10-20 it calls itself the sixth-largest US builder by revenue, in 26 of the top 50 MSAs. It runs a stated 100% land-light model: 52,574 lots controlled through finished-lot option and land bank option contracts at 2026-09-30 (before Beazer; $490M of lot deposits), and its deal deck showed about 87,900 pro forma lots, 78% optioned. At the Beazer closing it sold pre-acquisition Beazer land to Millrose for a $572.1M land bank facility (the deck had named Kennedy Lewis as the buyer), and it has said it will deleverage over 18 to 24 months and drop Beazer land deals that miss its return thresholds.

people.name: Patrick O. Zalupski
people.title: President, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Chairman of the Board of Directors

people.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 (signature page)
people.note: Founder and controlling shareholder. Company filings say he is heavily involved in origination, underwriting and structuring of all land investment activities, and he sits on the Asset Management Committee (the land capital-allocation committee). LP investor in DF Capital Fund II ($25.25M commitment) and Fund III ($50.3M) per the 2026 proxy. Sources conflict on DF Capital's investment committee: the FY2025 10-K and the live management page say he has served on it since April 2018, while the newer April 2026 proxy says he 'previously served'; the proxy is the later filing. Sole Chairman until 2026-07-13, when Rick Beckwitt became Co-Chairman. Also majority owner of the Tampa Bay Rays since September 2025.

Chief Accounting Officer / Controller: none named; the CFO signs as Principal Financial and Accounting Officer.

Regional land heads other than Matt Childers (Texas / Colorado / Arizona): job postings confirm a Regional VP of Land layer but name no one for the Southeast or Mid-Atlantic.

Series B preferred investors (12% convertible preferred, $675M across two closings) each hold a board observer right, but neither the investors nor any observer is named in the 8-K.
Builder magazine's 2025 Builder of the Year feature (which names more DFH leaders in captions): not read.
